literal: the man of Qi worries about the sky
meaning_long: worrying about things that will never happen
source: 《列子·天瑞》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
story: Ancient China, the small state of Qi. A nervous man is sure that one day the sky will fall on his head and the ground will crack open under his feet. He worries so much that he cannot eat or sleep, and even wears a cooking pot on his head as a helmet. His cheerful friend comes to visit and explains: the sky is just air, and the ground is solid everywhere, so nothing is going to fall or break. The man finally relaxes, laughs, and sleeps peacefully.
continuity: - THE WORRIER: thin, nervous man about 35, messy topknot, big worried eyes with dark circles under them, thin droopy mustache, faded slate-blue robe; in I1 and I3 he wears a round iron cooking pot on his head like a helmet.
- THE FRIEND: cheerful, stocky man about 40, round smiling face, short black beard, ochre robe, relaxed and calm.
- THE WORRIER'S HOME: a small village house with a courtyard, a low wooden table, a simple bed under a round window.
- SETTING: a peaceful ancient village with soft grey ink-wash hills, and a calm, ordinary sky with a few soft clouds.
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

Sunny, peaceful courtyard under a perfectly calm blue sky. The worrier crouches under the low wooden table with an iron cooking pot on his head, clutching an open paper umbrella, staring up at the harmless sky in pure terror, sweat drops flying. His friend stands beside the table looking down at him, puzzled, one eyebrow raised. Both faces clear. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.
The worrier stands in his courtyard looking straight up at the sky, biting his nails, eyes huge and anxious, shoulders hunched. (Only the worrier.)

His imagined nightmare, painted with swirling ink edges: the sky above the village cracks like a broken porcelain bowl, pieces of blue sky falling, the ground splitting into cracks, and the worrier, small, running in panic with the pot on his head. (Only the worrier.)
Night. The worrier sits at the low table in front of a full, untouched bowl of rice, dark circles under his eyes, staring nervously out of the round window at the night sky. (Only the worrier.)
Daytime in the courtyard: the friend smiles kindly and points up at the sky, explaining with an open hand. The worrier listens nervously, hugging himself.
The friend cheerfully stamps one foot on the solid ground and spreads his arms. The worrier looks down at the ground in surprise, starting to calm down.
Night: the worrier sleeps peacefully in his bed under the round window full of calm stars, a big happy smile, the iron pot set aside on the floor. (Only the worrier.)
The pot (background for the big title)

The iron cooking pot lying upside down on the grass of the courtyard in the lower half of the frame. The upper half is a calm, plain sky with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing in it (we place the big title there). No people.

A modern bedroom at night: the same WORRIER (thin, droopy mustache, dark circles) in slate-blue pajamas sits wide awake in bed, hugging his knees and sweating, staring at a wall calendar (plain grid, no numbers, no text) with one day circled far away at the bottom. No other people. No text, no logos, no screens.
lines: He was sure the sky would fall on his head.
This man worried all day, every day.
What if the sky falls? What if the ground breaks?
He could not eat. He could not sleep.
His friend said: the sky is just air.
And the ground is solid everywhere. Relax!
Finally, he smiled and slept like a baby.
The man of Qi worries about the sky.
It means worrying about things that will never happen.
Like losing sleep over a test that is a month away.
title: He was sure the sky would fall on his head ☁️ | 杞人忧天
desc: 杞人忧天 (qǐ rén yōu tiān) = worrying about things that will never happen. Ever done that? 👇
